investigation.method: manual review of the live website with NHS profile and selected repo evidence

headline: Rock Healthcare exposes one of the messiest access setups reviewed so far. The public site is a WordPress build, the visible patient-services hub pushes Accurx, live askmyGP links are still embedded on the site, conventional appointments and contact pages return 404, and the result feels more like an unstable collection of routes than a clear front door.

live_stack.label: Public website stack
evidence: The site exposes wp-content assets and WordPress API links.
Source assets include an understrap-child theme.

live_stack.label: Current online request platform
evidence: The homepage and online-services support page point patients to Accurx routes.
The support page links to daily urgent triage, repeat prescription and fit-note flows under accurx.nhs.uk.

live_stack.label: Legacy or parallel route still exposed on the site
evidence: The online-services support page still contains live askmyGP links.
The askmyGP intro route for code Y02755 still resolves.

current_routes.label: Accurx patient hub
notes: The site presents this as the main patient-services route for online access.

current_routes.label: Accurx urgent medical triage
notes: The support page says urgent health concerns needing same-day attention should be submitted here.
It says submissions are triaged on the day received.

current_routes.label: askmyGP route still exposed
notes: The site still surfaces askmyGP under Get Help Now.
That leaves patients with more than one branded online front door.

current_routes.label: Repeat prescriptions
notes: The prescriptions page says the easiest route is online and also offers NHS App, email and pharmacy ordering.
It says prescription requests are not accepted over the phone unless the patient is housebound or unable to use the listed methods.

current_routes.label: Phone route
notes: The homepage says telephone enquiries run between 8am and 6:30pm with the reception team.

complaints_and_feedback.headline: The complaints route exists, but the site architecture around it is still messy.

items.label: Complaints and compliments page
notes: The page says patients should contact the practice manager by telephone or in writing.
This route is clearer than the broken appointments and contact pages, but it still sits inside a cluttered site structure.

stale_or_conflicting_signals.label: Broken conventional navigation
notes: Common-looking routes such as /appointments and /contact-us return 404.
That makes the site feel less predictable than the clearer patient hub pages.

stale_or_conflicting_signals.label: Accurx plus askmyGP overlap
notes: The public site currently exposes both Accurx and askmyGP routes.
This may be intentional overlap, or it may be stale remnants, but either way it increases ambiguity.

gpps_2025_26.headline: Rock Healthcare is weak on the core contact metrics.

google_review_texts.headline: The captured review sample is polarized, but several recent negatives talk directly about digital access and booking failures.
notes: One recent review explicitly says the Accurx route is badly designed.
Other negative reviews describe booking mistakes, wrong-site appointments and unhelpful reception handling, even though some five-star reviews praise individual staff.

probably_true: Rock's problem looks less like the existence of Accurx alone and more like an incoherent access stack and messy public information architecture.
The concurrent askmyGP links are significant because they suggest either incomplete migration or too many entry points.
needs_follow_up: Whether askmyGP is truly still in active use or merely left exposed on the website.
Whether some of the missing public routes are deliberate and replaced by hub pages, or just poor site maintenance.
